sections.h2: What should a Mille Lacs County, MN seller check first on the tax side?
sections.html:
One combined Property Records and Taxation Office at 635 2nd Street SE in Milaca handles billing here, and the Assessor sits on the ground floor of the same historic courthouse. About 20,000 tax parcels fall under the county. Each real estate transfer goes through that office, where deed tax or mortgage registry tax is collected and the ownership record is changed.

The same office certifies whether taxes are paid, so it is the first stop for a house, cabin or lake lot. Learn which half-year payment is open, whether any older year is delinquent, and which class the parcel carries. Buyers ask about class, since a lakeshore parcel taxed as seasonal recreational is billed on a different basis than a year-round homestead.

  • Property Records and Taxation: 320-983-8310 for general questions, 320-983-8301 about redemption notices, and 320-983-8304 when the online tax database misbehaves.
  • Assessor: 320-983-8311 or assessor@millelacs.mn.gov for value and class questions.

sections.h2: Where is Mille Lacs County and why does the lake matter to a sale?
sections.html:
East central Minnesota is home to Mille Lacs County, named for Mille Lacs Lake (the French words mean thousand lakes). It was formed on May 23, 1857, and spans 682 square miles. About 109 of those, or 16%, are water. The Rum River drains south from the lake, and the county holds Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, Father Hennepin State Park and part of the Mille Lacs Indian Reservation.

Courthouse business happens in Milaca, while Princeton, which extends into Sherburne County, is the biggest city. Isle, Onamia, Foreston, Pease, Bock and Wahkon are the others. Students attend the Isle, Milaca, Ogilvie, Onamia or Princeton school district. The 2025 estimate is 27,753 people, a 4.8% rise over the 2020 base. In 2020 the county had 12,786 housing units and 17.2% stood vacant. Over 2020 to 2024, QuickFacts shows 77.9% of homes owner-occupied, a typical home value of $258,300, household income of $72,729 and a 32.0 minute average commute, the longest among McLeod, Meeker and Mille Lacs.

sections.h2: When is Mille Lacs County property tax due?
sections.html:
Each property type has its own schedule in the county FAQ.

  • Real property: May 15 and October 15.
  • Agricultural property: May 15 and November 15.
  • Mobile homes: August 31 and November 15.
  • Personal property: May 15, with one payment.

Real estate and personal property statements go out in March and must be mailed by March 31. Manufactured home statements follow in the first week of July. Each mortgage company gets its own listing, and escrowed owners still receive a statement for their files. A manufactured home parcel stays in the old owner's name until the certificate of title is transferred, and that transfer first requires every current and delinquent personal property tax to be paid.

sections.h2: How does Mille Lacs County classify cabins, farms and homes?
sections.html:
Class sets the rate applied to your value, and the Assessor publishes short definitions. These stand out for the area:

  • Residential homestead (1a): the primary residence of the owner or a qualifying relative.
  • Residential nonhomestead (4b): a home that is the primary residence of someone else, with no more than three livable units.
  • Seasonal recreational residential (4c): a secondary, weekend or vacation home that is no one's primary residence.
  • Seasonal commercial (4c): resorts and other income property open fewer than 250 days a year.
  • Rural vacant land (2b): unplatted, unimproved land of more than five acres.
  • Managed forest (2c): at least 20 unplatted, unimproved acres with a Forest Stewardship Plan.

A cabin owner whose buyer plans to live there year-round should talk through the change early, since homestead status ends at sale and the buyer must apply. For larger tracts, the Assessor adds that designated public roads are exempt and private roads and driveways are taxable.

sections.h2: What happens when Mille Lacs County taxes go delinquent?
sections.html:
Penalties add up monthly after each due date, yet a tax year is not delinquent until the next January 1. This is the county's sequence for a parcel that stays unpaid.

Mille Lacs County delinquent tax timeline (Mille Lacs County Auditor-Treasurer FAQ)
DateWhat happens
January 1 after the payable yearThe taxes are classified as delinquent and interest begins to accrue monthly
February 15Parcels still owing go on the delinquent list filed with the court administrator, and the owner is mailed a letter
On or before March 20First newspaper publication of the list
At least two weeks laterSecond publication, with paid parcels removed
Second Monday in MayJudgment is taken and the parcel is bid in for the state
Usually three years afterRedemption period ends in most cases

Someone unable to pay in full can sign a confession of judgment. It folds delinquent tax, special assessments, penalties, costs and interest into a single sum paid over 5 or 10 years, depending on class, and the plan is cancelled if current-year tax lapses. Notices of expiration of redemption are the last step before forfeiture. They go out by certified mail, the sheriff serves them, and the county paper prints them.

sections.h2: How can I pay Mille Lacs County property tax?
sections.html: The online portal finds statements by owner name, parcel ID, street address, or section, township and range. Paying there adds a processor fee: 2.35% on a card, with a $2.00 floor, or $2.00 on an e-check, and the county keeps none of it. Other payments go by mail to the Property Records and Taxation Office, 635 2nd Street SE, Milaca, MN 56353. A declined online payment is a question for your bank. If the database shows an error, try again in 15 minutes and then call 320-983-8304.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Mille Lacs County valuation?
sections.html:
Your Notice of Valuation and Classification comes in March, at least ten days ahead of the meeting in your township or city. The meeting details are printed at the bottom, and some jurisdictions run open book sessions with the assessor in place of a formal board.

The county suggests gathering proof such as a recent appraisal or comparable sales, having the Assessor review the data, then presenting at the local board in April or May in person, through a representative or by letter. Next comes an appointment with the county board in June, which is open only to owners who made the local appeal first. Anything still unresolved can go to the Minnesota Tax Court, with the petition filed before April 30 of the payable year.

For Tax Court, the county's instructions call for four copies of the petition and five of the tax statement. Serve the Assessor, the County Attorney and the Auditor-Treasurer, then file the original with the court administrator and pay the fee. Expect a trial date within a year.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks and refunds apply to Mille Lacs County owners?
sections.html:
The county's Assessor page says the homestead market value exclusion for taxes payable in 2025 peaked at $38,000 on a $95,000 home and ended for homes worth more than $517,200. It shrinks the taxable value of a homestead and therefore the net tax. Ask the Assessor for current figures.

Minnesota also pays an income-based homestead refund. The county does not handle it and routes questions to the Department of Revenue. A Form M1PR claim has to include a tax statement showing no delinquent tax on the homestead. August 15 is the due date, with late returns accepted until August 15 of the following year, and timely claims are paid in late September or early October. The Assessor is also collecting reassessment questionnaires for 2027, the year each property gets its physical review under the five-year cycle.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Mille Lacs County need to settle before closing?
sections.html:
Request a payoff for the open half and a certification of paid or unpaid tax from the Property Records and Taxation Office. Under Minnesota Statutes 272.12 a deed is not recorded until the auditor confirms no delinquent taxes and enters the transfer. Sales above $3,000 need a certificate of value (272.115), and homestead status drops off after a transfer until the buyer applies and qualifies.

The Assessor sends a sales verification questionnaire for sales in the county. The county uses verified sales to study the market and set values, and the state uses the same studies for refunds and aid payments.

faqs.q: What is the mailing address for a Mille Lacs County tax check?
faqs.a: Send it to the Property Records and Taxation Office, 635 2nd Street SE, Milaca, MN 56353, or pay through the online portal. Call 320-983-8310 with questions.

faqs.q: What are the Mille Lacs County tax due dates?
faqs.a: Real property is due May 15 and October 15, and agricultural property is due May 15 and November 15. Mobile homes are due August 31 and November 15, and personal property is due May 15.

faqs.q: What fees apply when paying Mille Lacs County taxes online?
faqs.a: Cards cost 2.35% with a $2.00 minimum, and e-checks cost $2.00. The processor collects both and the county gets nothing.

faqs.q: Is there an installment plan for back taxes in Mille Lacs County?
faqs.a: Yes. A confession of judgment spreads delinquent taxes, assessments, penalties, costs and interest across 5 or 10 years, provided current-year taxes keep getting paid.

faqs.q: Can I skip the local meeting and go straight to the Mille Lacs County board?
faqs.a: No. The June county meeting is open only after you raise the concern at the local board or open book meeting in April or May. Tax Court petitions are due before April 30.
